sections.title: Valuation Insights
sections.text: Costco generated [[COST.fact.revenue]] in annual revenue, growing [[COST.ratio.revenue_growth]] percent year‑over‑year, which underscores strong top‑line momentum. Its operating margin of [[COST.ratio.operating_margin]] percent signals modest profitability given the scale of its business, while the return on average equity of [[COST.ratio.return_on_average_equity]] percent demonstrates highly efficient capital deployment. The company’s balance sheet is lightly leveraged, with a debt‑to‑equity ratio of [[COST.ratio.debt_to_equity]] and a combined long‑term and current debt of [[COST.fact.long_term_debt]] plus [[COST.fact.current_debt]] respectively, indicating ample capacity to fund growth initiatives. Free cash flow of [[COST.ratio.free_cash_flow]] shows robust cash generation after capital expenditures, supporting dividend sustainability and share repurchases. However, the annual price‑to‑earnings multiple of [[COST.ratio.price_earnings]] suggests the market is pricing in a premium relative to earnings, reflecting expectations of continued growth and strong brand positioning. Overall, the blend of high ROE, low leverage, and strong free cash flow paints a picture of a financially resilient retailer, though valuation remains elevated.

insight.text: Costco’s debt‑to‑equity ratio of [[COST.ratio.debt_to_equity]] reflects a very low leverage profile, which cushions the company against interest‑rate pressure and provides flexibility for future strategic investments.
